_meta.half_life_warning: Regulatory facts in this file are VOLATILE BY DESIGN. Treat every entry as a dated snapshot; re-verify on cadence. All URLs marked [verify] have not been confirmed against a live source in this session.
_meta.tier4_note: LGU-level building-permit ledgers and on-the-ground enforcement practice are predominantly tier-4 (offline counter records, Facebook pages of city/municipal engineering offices, WhatsApp circulars among contractors). Automated harvesting does NOT close this; route to the local Office of the Building Official (OBO) or a licensed structural engineer (PRC-registered) for signed capture.
_meta.safety_stance: DETECTION and ROUTING with citations only. No evasion of codes or permits. No PII stored. This registry supports flagging approved-floor-count vs actual, missing licensed-engineer sign-off, and occupancy/structural red flags — then routing to the building official / authority.

sources.publisher: Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH)
issuance_types: National Structural Code of the Philippines (NSCP) adoption issuances
sources.access_method: PDF download from directory listing; no clean API known [verify]
sources.cadence: irregular; major updates tied to NSCP revision cycles [verify]
sources.cdc_needs: Manual re-check on each NSCP edition release and DPWH DO cycle; no delta feed — full-page diff required
sources.notes: DPWH oversees national structural and infrastructure standards. The National Structural Code of the Philippines (NSCP) — published by ASEP (Association of Structural Engineers of the Philippines) [verify] — is the technical backbone for allowable floor loads, seismic zone factors, and structural adequacy. NSCP 7th edition [verify edition number and year] is the current reference. DPWH does not directly issue building permits (that is LGU/OBO authority) but sets the technical standards that OBOs are required to apply under PD 1096 IRR.

sources.publisher: Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG)
issuance_types: Joint Circulars with DPWH and DICT on LGU compliance
Guidelines on LGU Building Official appointments
Directives on post-disaster building inspection protocols
sources.access_method: PDF listings on dilg.gov.ph; no structured API known [verify]
sources.cdc_needs: Full-page diff on MCs page; no feed — monitor issuance list page for changes
sources.notes: DILG supervises LGUs and can issue directives binding on city/municipal engineering offices and Offices of the Building Official. After a major collapse, DILG typically issues a memorandum ordering inspections nationwide. These are often the most operationally relevant issuances for detecting systemic violation patterns across jurisdictions. DILG Facebook page (facebook.com/DILG.Philippines [verify]) is used for public announcements and may carry material ahead of the website — tier 4 channel.

sources.publisher: Office of the Building Official (OBO) — Local Government Unit level
issuance_types: Building permits (BP) — approved floor count, occupancy classification
Fire safety clearance coordination records [BUREAU OF FIRE PROTECTION]
sources.access_method: COUNTER ONLY — most LGU OBOs have no public digital portal for permit record lookup as of 2025 [verify]; some metro LGUs have partial online verification systems
sources.format: Paper ledger / internal electronic record; not publicly addressable
sources.cadence: Continuous (per permit application); no public feed
sources.cdc_needs: NOT applicable via automation — requires in-person FOI request or formal query to the LGU OBO; human-router path only
sources.notes: This is the most operationally critical source for detecting approved-floor-count vs actual-floor-count discrepancies (the Angeles City collapse scenario). The building permit issued by the LGU OBO specifies the approved number of stories/floors. The gap between the approved permit and as-built reality is the primary red flag. However, this data is overwhelmingly tier-4: no national permit database is publicly queryable [verify]; some cities have begun digitization but completeness is low [verify]. A licensed structural engineer or OBO staff member performing a site visit is the authoritative verification path. Route to: the LGU's Office of the Building Official, the Philippine Institute of Certified Public Accountants for permit fees in question [check], or the DPWH regional office overseeing the LGU.
sources.routing_authority: LGU Office of the Building Official; DPWH Regional Office; DILG (for systemic LGU non-compliance)

sources.publisher: Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) — Board of Civil Engineering / Board of Architecture
issuance_types: Licensed Structural Engineer designation [verify — check if 'structural engineer' is a separate PRC-regulated specialty or a sub-specialty of civil engineering in PH]
sources.access_method: Online verification portal for license status [verify URL and coverage]; PDF resolutions on prc.gov.ph
sources.cadence: License registry: near-real-time for suspensions/revocations [verify]; resolutions: periodic
sources.cdc_needs: Periodic re-check of license status for specific professionals cited in permits; monitor for revocation orders; no bulk delta feed known [verify]
sources.notes: Under PD 1096 and the IRR, building permit applications above a certain floor count or structural complexity require sign-off by a licensed structural engineer and/or architect. The PRC registry is the authoritative source for verifying whether the signing professional holds a valid, unsuspended license. This is an accountability_or_license signal: a model cannot hold or verify a PRC license — only the PRC registry can. A permit signed by a lapsed or revoked license is itself a red flag. PRC license verification should be a mandatory gate in the If Statement (rule) component for high-rise building permit screening.

sources.publisher: National Building Code of the Philippines (PD 1096) and Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR)
sources.base_url: https://www.dpwh.gov.ph [verify — PD 1096 text; also on lawphil.net and chan robles virtual law library]
issuance_types: IRR of PD 1096 — implementing rules [verify current revision date]
DPWH Department Orders that amend or supplement the IRR
Referential technical standards (NSCP, NFPA, ASTM adoption)
sources.access_method: PDF — lawphil.net, chan robles, DPWH; no structured API; text is in English
sources.format: PDF / HTML (secondary aggregators lawphil.net, chan robles)
sources.cadence: PD 1096 is stable (1977); IRR amendments are event-driven — check DPWH DOs [verify last IRR amendment date]
sources.cdc_needs: Monitor DPWH DO page for IRR amendments; the base PD 1096 text is stable but IRR Section references shift with revisions — version every extract
sources.notes: PD 1096 and its IRR are the primary legal basis for building permits, floor-count approval, occupancy classification, and licensed professional requirements in the Philippines. Key provisions for violation detection: Section 301 (permit requirement) [verify], Section 307 (Certificate of Occupancy) [verify], Section 207 (duties of the Building Official) [verify], Rule VIII on structural requirements [verify rule numbering in current IRR]. The IRR specifies which floor counts / use categories require a licensed structural engineer's signature. Any detection If Statement citing these must include the specific section number AND the IRR version date — regulatory facts are volatile and clause numbers shift between revisions. This source is tier-3: the text exists on stable public URLs but requires OCR or structured extraction; secondary aggregators (lawphil.net) provide searchable HTML.

issuance_types: Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514) implementing rules [verify]
BFP circulars on occupancy/high-rise fire safety requirements
sources.access_method: PDF on bfp.gov.ph; FSIC verification is counter-level [verify if any online lookup exists]
sources.cdc_needs: Monitor BFP circulars page; individual FSIC verification requires human-router / OBO coordination
sources.notes: The Fire Code (RA 9514 and its IRR [verify]) requires a valid FSIC as a prerequisite for Certificate of Occupancy and for buildings above certain occupancy thresholds. An illegally added floor may not have been inspected for fire safety. BFP coordination is a required gate in the routing action: flag missing or expired FSIC alongside the floor-count discrepancy. BFP also maintains Facebook presence (facebook.com/BFPOfficial [verify]) for public announcements — tier-4 channel not suitable for automated harvesting.

sources.publisher: Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) — Occupational Safety and Health Center (OSHC)
issuance_types: Occupational Safety and Health Standards (OSHS) — RA 11058 IRR
Department Order 198 (s. 2018) — implementing RA 11058 [verify DO number]
Toolbox talk / safety officer accreditation requirements
sources.access_method: PDF on oshc.dole.gov.ph and dole.gov.ph; paginated listing; no API
sources.cadence: OSHS amendments: infrequent but material; monitor DOLE DO page
sources.cdc_needs: Monitor DOLE DO issuance list for OSHS-related amendments
sources.notes: RA 11058 (Occupational Safety and Health Standards) and its IRR (DO 198 s. 2018 [verify]) require construction sites above certain size to have an accredited safety officer. Workers trapped in a collapse with no certified safety officer on site is a compound violation: building code violation (floor count) + OSH violation (safety officer requirement, emergency procedures). The OSHC/DOLE channel is relevant for routing worker-safety aspects of a building collapse investigation to the correct authority (DOLE regional office) alongside the building-code routing (OBO/DPWH).

sources.publisher: LGU City/Municipal Engineering Office + OBO Social Media (Facebook pages)
issuance_types: Mayor's office announcements on building violations
sources.access_method: Facebook page (login-walled for scraping; publicly viewable in browser); WhatsApp broadcast to contractors
sources.format: Social post (image, text, video); screenshot-forwarded circular
sources.cdc_needs: NOT applicable via automation — monitor via human subscriber; posts can be edited/deleted without notice; no canonical record
sources.notes: In practice, informal enforcement announcements, local stop-work orders, and permit-related notices for many Philippine LGUs are first (and sometimes only) published on the local government's Facebook page or via WhatsApp group chats of the local engineers/contractors network. This is the canonical tier-4 channel: crawler-inaccessible for bulk harvesting, ephemeral, editable. A verified-publisher path (a licensed structural engineer or OBO staff member who is a subscriber) is required to convert this channel into a citable fact. The human-router component must explicitly handle this channel with signed capture and provenance.
sources.routing_authority: LGU OBO staff; licensed civil/structural engineer with local relationships

durability_assessment.rationale: LGU building-permit records (approved floor count) are overwhelmingly tier-4 or tier-5 (counter-only / human site visit). PRC license verification is tier-2 (usable but no delta feed). The base law text (PD 1096) is tier-3 but volatile via IRR amendments. On-the-ground practice (what the OBO actually enforces, informal price of compliance) is tacit local knowledge — never written. All primary lift reasons are structural. The gap will not close when the next model ships because the authoritative source of floor-count approval is a paper ledger at a counter, and only a body (licensed engineer site visit) can verify the as-built count.
